title: Unit 1 Stand-alone 2: Clinical Manifestations (Signs vs. Symptoms)

question.stem: The nurse is completing an admission assessment on a client presenting with acute pulmonary disease. Which of the following documented assessment findings represents an objective clinical sign rather than a subjective symptom?

options.text: Client states, 'I have felt short of breath for the past three days.'
Auscultation of bilateral expiratory wheezes in both lower pulmonary lobes
Client describes a sharp, stabbing retrosternal chest pain rated 7 out of 10
Client reports feeling dizzy, fatigued, and nauseated after walking

question.preamble: The triage nurse is documenting physical assessment data in the electronic health record.
question.explanation: A clinical sign is an objective finding that can be directly observed, measured, or verified by the healthcare provider through physical examination, diagnostic tools, or laboratory measurement (e.g., auscultated wheezes, blood pressure, fever). Subjective symptoms are personal perceptions or sensations verbalized exclusively by the client (e.g., dyspnea, nausea, fatigue, pain intensity).

leftContent.intro: An 64-year-old client presents to the emergency department accompanied by a spouse, reporting worsening respiratory difficulty over the last 72 hours.

tabs.title: Triage Intake
tabs.content:
Chief Complaint: Client reports severe shortness of breath and pleuritic chest soreness.
Triage Vitals: T 37.8° C, P 108 beats/min, RR 26 breaths/min, BP 142/86 mm Hg, SpO2 89% on room air.
Physical Assessment: Tachypneic with intercostal retractions; coarse expiratory wheezes audible bilaterally.
